label: lem:Pfg-explicit
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Pfg-explicit}
Assume all parameters are real and \(k\ge1\). Let \(P_{fg,n}\) be as in Definition~\ref{def:Pfg}, and put
\[
c=f^{2}(1,k)(k-1),\quad d=f^{2}(k,k)(k-1),\quad
a,b=\frac{\lambda-g(k)\pm\sqrt{(\lambda-g(k))^{2}-4d}}{2},
\]
\[
P_{fg,0}=\lambda-g(1),\qquad
P_{fg,1}=[\lambda-g(k)][\lambda-g(1)]-c.
\]
If \(a\ne b\), then
\[
P_{fg,n}
=\frac{(\lambda-g(1))(a^{n+1}-b^{n+1})-c(a^{n}-b^{n})}{a-b}.
\]
If \(a=b\ne0\), then
\[
P_{fg,n}=\left(P_{fg,0}+\left(\frac{P_{fg,1}}{a}-P_{fg,0}\right)n\right)a^{n},
\qquad a=\frac{\lambda-g(k)}{2}.
\]
If \(a=b=0\), then \(P_{fg,n}=0\ (n\ge2)\).

For \(L/L^{+}\), \(g(1)=1\), \(g(k)=k\), \(f^{2}(1,k)=f^{2}(k,k)=1\), so \(c=d=k-1\), and for \(a\ne b\),
\[
P_{L,n}
=\frac{(\lambda-1)(a^{n+1}-b^{n+1})-(k-1)(a^{n}-b^{n})}{a-b},
\quad
a,b=\frac{\lambda-k\pm\sqrt{(\lambda-k)^{2}-4(k-1)}}{2}.
\]
With \(r=k-1\), \(s=\sqrt r\), \(x_L=(\lambda-k)/(2s)\),
\[
P_{L,n}=r^{(n+1)/2}\bigl(U_{n+1}(x_L)+sU_n(x_L)\bigr),
\]
where \(U_n\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind, defined by the recurrence
\[
U_0(x)=1,\quad U_1(x)=2x,\quad U_{n+1}(x)=2xU_n(x)-U_{n-1}(x)\ (n\ge1),
\]
and given explicitly by
\[
U_n(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}(-1)^j\binom{n-j}{j}(2x)^{n-2j}.
\]
head: environment

label: thm:D
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:D}
For \(n\ge2\), the characteristic polynomial of the weighted adjacency-degree matrix of \(D_{n,k}\) is
\[
\phi(A_{fg}(D_{n,k}),\lambda)
= \bigl( P_{fg,n} - f^2(k,k) P_{fg,n-2} \bigr)
P_{fg,n-1}^{k-1}
\prod_{j=0}^{n-2} P_{fg,j}^{k (k-1)^{n-j-2} (k-2)}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The weighted adjacency-degree matrix of \(D_{n,k}\) is
\[
A_{fg}(D_{n,k})=
\begin{pmatrix}
g(1)I_{N_{0}} & f(1,k)J_{m_{0}} &  &  \\
f(1,k)J_{m_{0}}^T & g(k)I_{N_{1}} & f(k,k)J_{m_{1}} & \\
& \ddots & \ddots & \\
& & f(k,k)J_{m_{n-1}}^T & g(k)I_{N_{n}}
\end{pmatrix},
\]
where \(J_{m_s}\) is the \(N_s\times N_{s+1}\) 0-1 matrix
\(
J_{m_s}=I_{N_{s+1}}\otimes \mathbf{1}_{m_s},
\)
with \(\mathbf{1}_{m_s}\) the all-ones column vector of length \(m_s\). Thus each column of \(J_{m_s}\) contains exactly \(m_s\) ones, and
\(
J_{m_s}^T J_{m_s}=m_s I_{N_{s+1}}.
\)
By block elimination, adding \(\frac{f(1,k)}{\lambda-g(1)}J_{m_0}^T\) times the first row to the second row yields
\[
|\lambda I-A_{fg}(D_{n,k})|
=
\begin{vmatrix}
P_{fg,0}I_{N_0} & -f(1,k)J_{m_0} & & \\
& \frac{P_{fg,1}}{P_{fg,0}}I_{N_1} & -f(k,k)J_{m_1} & \\
& & \ddots & \\
& & & \frac{P_{fg,n}-f^2(k,k)P_{fg,n-2}}{P_{fg,n-1}}I_{N_n}
\end{vmatrix}.
\]
Repeating this elimination gives the result.
\qed
head: environment

label: thm:B
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:B}
For \(n\ge2\), the characteristic polynomial of the weighted adjacency-degree matrix of \(B_{n,k}\) is
\[
\phi(A_{fg}(B_{n,k}),\lambda)
= \biggl( \bigl( \lambda - g(k-1) \bigr) P_{fg,n-1}
- f^2(k-1,k)(k-1) P_{fg,n-2} \biggr)
\prod_{j=0}^{n-1} P_{fg,j}^{(k-1)^{n-j-1}(k-2)}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is analogous to that of Theorem~\ref{thm:D}. The block elimination yields the end factor
\[
(\lambda-g(k-1))P_{fg,n-1}-f^2(k-1,k)(k-1)P_{fg,n-2}
\]
and the product over \(j=0,\dots,n-1\) with exponents \((k-1)^{n-j-1}(k-2)\).
\qed

label: prop:cheb-roots
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:cheb-roots}
Let \(r=k-1\), \(s=\sqrt r\). For \(L/L^+\), put \(x_L=(\lambda-k)/(2s)\). Then
\(P_{L,j}=0\) iff \(U_{j+1}(x_L)+sU_j(x_L)=0\). This equation is equivalent to
\[
\sin((j+2)\theta)+s\sin((j+1)\theta)=0
\quad (x_L=\cos\theta,\ 0<\theta<\pi),
\]
\[
s\sinh((j+1)t)=\sinh((j+2)t)
\quad (x_L=-\cosh t,\ t>0),
\]
and has no solution for \(x_L>1\); the cases \(x_L=\pm1\) are checked directly. Moreover,
\[
P_{L,n}-P_{L,n-2}
=r^{(n-1)/2}\lambda\bigl(sU_n(x_L)-U_{n-1}(x_L)\bigr),
\]
so its roots are \(\lambda=0\) and those of \(sU_n(x_L)=U_{n-1}(x_L)\).

For \(A_\alpha\) with \(\alpha\ne1\), put
\(
\beta=1-\alpha,\quad
s_\alpha=\beta\sqrt r,\quad
x_\alpha=\frac{\lambda-\alpha k}{2s_\alpha},\quad
\delta_\alpha=\frac{\alpha\sqrt r}{\beta}.
\)
Then
\(
P_{\alpha,j}
=s_\alpha^{j+1}
\bigl(U_{j+1}(x_\alpha)+\delta_\alpha U_j(x_\alpha)\bigr),
\)
and \(P_{\alpha,j}=0\) iff
\(U_{j+1}(x_\alpha)+\delta_\alpha U_j(x_\alpha)=0\).
The case \(\alpha=1\) gives \(A_\alpha=D\).

In general the equations are not equidistant cosine equations; explicit cosine formulas exist only for the factors \(P_{A,j}\) of the adjacency matrix and for the \(L/L^+\) end factor of \(B_{n,k}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:Pfg-explicit},
\(
P_{L,j}=r^{(j+1)/2}\bigl(U_{j+1}(x_L)+sU_j(x_L)\bigr),
\)
so \(P_{L,j}=0\) iff \(U_{j+1}(x_L)+sU_j(x_L)=0\).
The trigonometric form is obtained from \(U_j(\cos\theta)=\sin((j+1)\theta)/\sin\theta\).
\qed
head: environment

label: cor:D-L+
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The factorization follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:D} with the \(L/L^{+}\) parameters. The Chebyshev form of \(P_{L,n}-P_{L,n-2}\) is given in Proposition~\ref{prop:cheb-roots}. The multiplicities are read directly from the exponents in the factorization.
\qed
head: environment

label: cor:B-L+
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:B-L+}
The eigenvalues of the characteristic polynomial of \(L^{+}(B_{n,k})\) are as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the roots of \(H_{B,L}=(\lambda-(k-1))P_{L,n-1}-(k-1)P_{L,n-2}
=r^{n/2}\lambda U_n(x_L)\) are \(\lambda=0\) and
\(
\lambda=k+2s\cos\frac{\ell\pi}{n+1}, (\ell=1,\ldots,n),
\)
each being a simple root of \(H_{B,L}\). 
\item the roots of \(P_{L,j}\) are \(\lambda=k+2s x\), where \(x\) is a real root of
\(
U_{j+1}(x)+sU_j(x)=0
\) for \(j=0,\ldots,n-1\).
Each such root contributes multiplicity \((k-1)^{n-j-1}(k-2)\) to the full characteristic polynomial.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The end factor identity follows from the Chebyshev form of \(P_{L,n}\). Its roots are \(0\) and \(k+2s\cos(\ell\pi/(n+1))\), \(\ell=1,\ldots,n\), each simple as a root of \(H_{B,L}\). The remaining factors are treated as in Corollary~\ref{cor:D-L+}; coincidences between roots of different factors are counted by adding multiplicities. 
\qed

label: thm:gershgorin
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:gershgorin}
Let \(A=(a_{ij})\) be an \(N\times N\) complex matrix. For each \(i=1,\dots,N\), define the Gershgorin disc
\(
D_i:=\left\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\ |z-a_{ii}|\le R_i\right\},
R_i:=\sum_{j\ne i}|a_{ij}|.
\)
Then every eigenvalue of \(A\) lies in the union \(\bigcup_{i=1}^N D_i\). Moreover, if a disc \(D_i\) is disjoint from the remaining discs, then it contains exactly one eigenvalue of \(A\).
head: environment

label: prop:psd
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:psd}
If for every vertex \(v\),
\(
g(d_v)\ge \sum_{u\sim v}|f(d_v,d_u)|,
\)
then \(A_{fg}\) is positive semidefinite. Consequently,
\(
E(A_{fg})=\operatorname{tr}(A_{fg})=\sum_{v\in V}g(d_v).
\)
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:gershgorin}, every eigenvalue of \(A_{fg}\) lies in the union of the discs
\[
D_v=\left\{z:\ |z-g(d_v)|\le R_v\right\},
\qquad
R_v=\sum_{u\sim v}|f(d_v,d_u)|.
\]
If \(g(d_v)\ge R_v\) for every \(v\), then each disc lies in the closed right half-plane, since \(\operatorname{Re} z\ge g(d_v)-R_v\ge 0\). Hence every eigenvalue of \(A_{fg}\) is nonnegative, i.e., \(A_{fg}\) is positive semidefinite. The energy equality then follows from \(E(A)=\sum_i|\lambda_i|=\sum_i\lambda_i=\operatorname{tr}(A)\) for a positive semidefinite matrix.
\qed
head: environment

label: cor:energy-eq
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:energy-eq}
The following energy equalities hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(L^+\): \(g(d)=d\), \(f=1\). The Gershgorin condition reduces to \(d_v\ge d_v\), so \(L^+\) is positive semidefinite and \(E(L^+)=2|E|\).
\item \(L\): \(g(d)=d\), \(f=-1\). Again \(d_v\ge d_v\), so \(L\) is positive semidefinite and \(E(L)=2|E|\). For bipartite graphs \(L\) and \(L^+\) are cospectral, so the two energies coincide.
\item \(A_\alpha\): \(g(d)=\alpha d\), \(f=1-\alpha\). The Gershgorin condition becomes \(\alpha d_v\ge |1-\alpha|d_v\iff \alpha\ge \tfrac12\). Hence for \(\alpha\ge \tfrac12\),
\[
E(A_\alpha)=\operatorname{tr}(A_\alpha)=\alpha\sum_v d_v=2\alpha|E|.
\]
In particular, at \(\alpha=\tfrac12\), \(A_{1/2}=\tfrac12 L^+\), so \(E(A_{1/2})=|E|\).
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
For \(L^{+}\) and \(L\), the energy equals \(2|E|\) by positive semidefiniteness,
as shown in Corollary~\ref{cor:energy-eq}. The Chebyshev equations in
Corollaries~\ref{cor:D-L+} and~\ref{cor:B-L+} locate the eigenvalues and give
their multiplicities, but they do not by themselves provide a complete explicit
sum over \(\theta\in(0,\pi)\), because some roots may correspond to \(|x|>1\).
For the energy, the trace argument is sufficient.
head: environment

label: rmk:few-eigen
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk:few-eigen}
In the nondegenerate case \(s\ne0\) and \(x\in(-1,1)\), the roots of different factors are determined by different Chebyshev boundary equations. Coincidences can occur only when these equations admit a common solution; this requires special algebraic relations among the parameters. For the adjacency matrix, the coincidences are exactly those of the Chebyshev zeros \(U_{j+1}(x)=0\).
head: environment

label: thm:energy-bound
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:energy-bound}
For any graph \(G\) and any real symmetric \(A_{fg}\),
\[
E(A_{fg})\le \sqrt{N\operatorname{tr}(A_{fg}^2)},\qquad N=|V|.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality applied to the eigenvalues of \(A_{fg}\),
\[
\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^N|\lambda_i|\Bigr)^2
\le N\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i^2
=N\operatorname{tr}(A_{fg}^2).
\]
Taking square roots gives the claim.
\qed
head: environment

label: thm:koolen-moulton
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:koolen-moulton}
For any graph \(G\) and any real symmetric \(A_{fg}\) with \(g\ge0\) and \(f\ge0\), assume that \(T^2\ge NC\), where
\[
N=|V|,\qquad
T=\operatorname{tr}(A_{fg})+2S,\qquad
C=\operatorname{tr}(A_{fg}^2),\qquad
S=\sum_{v_i v_j\in E} f(d_i,d_j).
\]
Then
\[
E(A_{fg})\le \frac{T}{N}
+\sqrt{(N-1)\Bigl(C-\Bigl(\frac{T}{N}\Bigr)^2\Bigr)}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_N\) be the eigenvalues of \(A_{fg}\). Since \(A_{fg}\) is nonnegative and nonzero, \(\lambda_1>0\). Write \(E(A_{fg})=\lambda_1+\sum_{i=2}^N|\lambda_i|\). By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality applied to the \((N-1)\)-tuple \((\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_N)\),
\[
\sum_{i=2}^N|\lambda_i|
\le\sqrt{(N-1)\sum_{i=2}^N\lambda_i^2}
=\sqrt{(N-1)\Bigl(C-\lambda_1^2\Bigr)}.
\]
Hence \(E(A_{fg})\le \varphi(\lambda_1)\), where \(\varphi(x):=x+\sqrt{(N-1)(C-x^2)}\). Next we bound \(\lambda_1\) from below. By the Rayleigh quotient characterization of the largest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix~\cite[Theorem 4.2.2]{HornJohnson2013}, taking the unit vector \(\mathbf{u}=\mathbf{1}/\sqrt{N}\) gives
\[
\lambda_1\ge \mathbf{u}^TA_{fg}\mathbf{u}
=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i,j}(A_{fg})_{ij}
=\frac{\operatorname{tr}(A_{fg})+2S}{N}
=\frac{T}{N}.
\]
Since \(g\ge0\) and \(f\ge0\), all entries of \(A_{fg}\) are nonnegative, so \(T\ge0\). We now show that \(\varphi\) is decreasing on \([\sqrt{C/N},\sqrt{C}]\). Indeed,
\[
\varphi'(x)=1-\frac{(N-1)x}{\sqrt{(N-1)(C-x^2)}},
\]
and \(\varphi'(x)\le0\) iff \((N-1)(C-x^2)\le (N-1)^2x^2\iff C\le Nx^2\iff x\ge\sqrt{C/N}\). Thus \(\varphi\) is decreasing on \([\sqrt{C/N},\sqrt{C}]\). By Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
T^2=\Bigl(\sum_{i,j}(A_{fg})_{ij}\Bigr)^2
\le N^2\sum_{i,j}(A_{fg})_{ij}^2=N^2C,
\]
so \(T/N\le\sqrt C\). Hence \(T/N\in[\sqrt{C/N},\sqrt{C}]\), and the assumption \(T^2\ge NC\) gives \(T/N\ge\sqrt{C/N}\). Therefore \(\varphi(\lambda_1)\le \varphi(T/N)\). Substituting the definition of \(\varphi\),
\[
E(A_{fg})\le \frac{T}{N}
+\sqrt{(N-1)\Bigl(C-\Bigl(\frac{T}{N}\Bigr)^2\Bigr)}.
\]
This proves the claim.
\qed
